filament.name: Proto-pasta High Temp Carbon Fiber PLA

heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 easily achieves the safe max speed of 155 mm/s constrained by a 13 mm³/s volumetric flow limit on Proto-pasta High Temp Carbon Fiber PLA. However, the stock stainless steel nozzle must be upgraded to a hardened steel hotend assembly to prevent rapid bore wear and extrusion failure.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate cleaned with isopropyl alcohol; no glue stick required at 60°C.
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 13 mm³/s in the filament settings to maintain extrusion consistency below 155 mm/s.
Enable Wipe While Retracting (set to 2 mm) to prevent stringing and nozzle buildup caused by stiff carbon fibers.
Adjust Pressure Advance (PA) to approximately 0.022-0.026 via OrcaSlicer calibration to account for carbon fiber stiffness.
Set Wall Generator to Arachne with a minimum wall line width of 0.45 mm for improved layer bonding and fiber alignment.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clogs or rapid under-extrusion mid-print
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Carbon fiber agglomeration in the 0.4mm orifice or abrasive wear on the stock stainless steel nozzle tip.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Install an official Bambu Lab hardened steel 0.4mm or 0.6mm hotend, and increase nozzle temperature to 225°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Surface fuzziness, brittleness, and poor layer adhesion
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Moisture absorption by the PLA base resin reducing polymer chain integrity during melt extrusion.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament in a dedicated filament dryer at 50°C for 6 to 8 hours prior to printing.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Corner warping or part detaching from the build plate
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive early cooling fan speed or oily fingerprint residue on the textured PEI sheet.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Wash the build plate with warm water and dish soap, set bed temperature to 60°C, and keep part cooling off for the first 3 layers.

faq.question: Can I print Proto-pasta HT-CF PLA with the stock Bambu Lab A1 hotend?
faq.answer: No, the stock hotend uses a stainless steel nozzle which will quickly erode from the chopped carbon fibers, enlarging the orifice and ruining print tolerances within a few hundred grams.

faq.question: Is an enclosure required to print this high-temp carbon fiber PLA on the A1?
faq.answer: No, an enclosure is not required; because it is PLA-based, it prints reliably on the open-frame A1 without chamber heating, which could actually cause heat creep.

faq.question: Does Proto-pasta HT-CF PLA work inside the Bambu Lab AMS Lite?
faq.answer: Yes, but prolonged usage of abrasive carbon fiber filaments can cause groove wear on the AMS Lite PTFE funnel guides over time, so inspect guides periodically.

faq.question: How do I achieve the high-temperature resistance advertised by Proto-pasta?
faq.answer: The printed part must be annealed (heat-treated) in a controlled oven at 95°C to 110°C for roughly 30 minutes to crystallize the amorphous PLA structure.
